A more rational approach would be to evaluate the product line based on its **current and future potential**, not on how much has already been spent. If the product is not performing well and there is no strong evidence it will improve, continuing to pour resources into it may lead to even greater losses. Decisions should be based on **expected future returns**, not on the desire to justify past expenditures.

In short, the argument is logically flawed and risks perpetuating a losing strategy simply to avoid acknowledging a past mistake.
